normalizationHints.sum: Shares of the raw values; criterion types are not used.
normalizationHints.minmax: Scaled to 0 to 1 first, cost reversed; negatives allowed.

normalizationHints.linearMax: The best value of each criterion becomes 1; cost uses min / x.
normalizationHints.sum: Each criterion becomes shares of its column total; cost uses 1 / x.

aggregationHints.eigenvector: Saaty's right principal eigenvector (A w = λmax w); matches the original AHP literature.
aggregationHints.geometric: Normalized row geometric means; equals the eigenvector for 3 criteria and solves in closed form.

aggregationHints.eigenvector: Saaty's right principal eigenvector (A p = λmax p) for pairwise criteria; matches the original AHP literature.
aggregationHints.geometric: Normalized row geometric means for pairwise criteria; equals the eigenvector for 3 alternatives and solves in closed form.

formulaHints.roc: Harmonic tail sum 1 / n · Σ 1 / k; centroid of the ordered weight simplex (Barron and Barrett 1996).
formulaHints.rs: Linear decay 2(n + 1 - r) / (n(n + 1)); flattest spread across ranks (Stillwell et al. 1981).
formulaHints.rr: Normalized reciprocal (1 / r) / H_n; steepest top-rank concentration (Stillwell et al. 1981).

stepRatioHints.moderate: Each criterion is 15% less important than the one above it (k = 1.15, q_j = q_{j-1} / 1.15).
stepRatioHints.gentle: Each criterion is 10% less important than the one above it (k = 1.10, flatter weight decay).
stepRatioHints.steep: Each criterion is 25% less important than the one above it (k = 1.25, steeper top-rank concentration).

preferenceFunctionHints.v-shape: Preference grows linearly from 0 to the column range; gives the same order as a min-max weighted sum.
preferenceFunctionHints.usual: Any positive difference counts as full preference (1); gives the same order as a weighted Borda count.
preferenceFunctionHints.level: Differences up to 20% of the column range are ignored, up to 60% count as 0.5, and larger differences count as 1.
preferenceFunctionHints.gaussian: Smooth S-shaped preference curve with inflection point at half the column range.

discordanceScaleHints.global: Roy (1968): divides every deficit by the largest span across all criteria; assumes a common scale.
discordanceScaleHints.range: Divides each deficit by its own criterion range (max - min), so mixed units are comparable.

thresholdPresetOptions.standard: Standard (q = 10%, p = 25% of range, no veto)
thresholdPresetOptions.strict: Strict (q = 5%, p = 15% of range, no veto)
thresholdPresetOptions.veto: With veto (q = 10%, p = 25%, v = 60% of range)

thresholdPresetHints.standard: Gaps up to 10% of the column range are indifferent, up to 25% build partial preference, and larger gaps give strict preference without veto.
thresholdPresetHints.strict: Tighter indifference (5%) and preference (15%) zones on each column range without veto.
thresholdPresetHints.veto: Adds a veto threshold at 60% of the column range so a large deficit on one criterion cuts credibility σ(a, b) down to 0.

methodHint.critic: Objective weights from how much each criterion varies and how much it disagrees with the others.
methodHint.entropy: Objective weights from how unevenly each criterion's values are spread over the alternatives.
methodHint.equal: Every criterion gets the same weight.
methodHint.manual: Enter your own weights. They must be 0 or more and sum to 1.
methodHint.sd: Objective weights from how widely each criterion's values spread over the alternatives.
methodHint.merec: Objective weights from how much the alternatives' overall performance drops when each criterion is removed. Every value must be above 0.
methodHint.lopcow: Objective weights from the log ratio of each criterion's root-mean-square to its sample standard deviation after min-max scaling.
methodHint.cilos: Objective weights from the impact loss other criteria suffer when each criterion's best alternative is chosen, solved by F w = 0. Every value must be above 0.
methodHint.bwm: Pick the most and least important criterion, then compare every other with these two (1‑9); 2n - 3 answers give the weights.
methodHint.ahp: Compare the criteria two at a time on the 1‑9 scale; all n(n - 1) / 2 answers give the weights and the consistency ratio CR.
methodHint.roc: Subjective weights from the importance order of the criteria (column 1 most important to column n least important), via ROC, Rank Sum or Rank Reciprocal.
methodHint.swara: Subjective weights from step-down importance ratios s_j between adjacent criteria in column order (k_j = 1 + s_j, q_j = q_{j-1} / k_j).

weights.normalizeHint: Divides each weight by the total, so the weights sum to 1.
weights.sumError: Weights sum to {{value}}, they must sum to 1.

methodHint.topsis: Ranks the alternatives by their distance from an ideal and a negative-ideal solution.
methodHint.saw: Weights the rescaled values of each criterion and adds them up.
methodHint.ahp-ranking: Synthesizes global priority P from criterion weights and local alternative priorities (table shares or 1‑9 pairwise comparisons).
methodHint.vikor: Looks for a compromise between the best total (S) and the smallest worst regret (R); a lower Q is better.
methodHint.edas: Scores each alternative by how far it lies above and below the average of all alternatives; a higher AS is better.
methodHint.waspas: Blends a weighted sum with a weighted product, which punishes a very weak value harder; a higher Q is better.
methodHint.copras: Adds up each alternative's weighted share of the benefit criteria plus a bonus that grows as its cost share shrinks; a higher Q is better.
methodHint.marcos: Measures each weighted total against an imaginary ideal and anti-ideal row; a higher f(K) is better, in the same order as SAW (Linear).
methodHint.cocoso: Reads a weighted sum S and a power sum P three ways and combines them; a higher k is better. Zeros and negative values are allowed.
methodHint.mabac: Adds up how far each alternative lies above or below a border, the geometric mean of every criterion; a higher S is better, in the same order as a min-max weighted sum. Zeros and negative values are allowed.
methodHint.moora: Divides each value by the Euclidean length of its column, adds the weighted benefit ratios and subtracts the weighted cost ratios; a higher y is better. Zeros and negative values are allowed.
methodHint.aras: Prepends an optimal row, adds up each alternative's weighted shares of the m + 1 column totals and divides by the optimal row's total; a higher K is better.
methodHint.codas: Scores each alternative by its Euclidean and Taxicab distances from the negative-ideal point, compared across every pair; a higher H is better.
methodHint.promethee-ii: Compares every pair of alternatives on each criterion with a preference function and subtracts the entering flow from the leaving flow; a higher φ is better. Zeros and negative values are allowed.
methodHint.electre-i: Tests every pair of alternatives for majority concordance (C ≥ ĉ) and bounded discordance (D ≤ d̂) to find the outranking kernel K, and ranks alternatives by normalized net concordance minus net discordance Φ. Zeros and negative values are allowed.
methodHint.electre-iii: Tests each pair with indifference, preference and veto thresholds to build fuzzy credibility σ(a, b) and distills descending and ascending rankings; a higher net credibility Φ is better. Zeros and negative values are allowed.

topsis.title: Distances to A+ and A−
topsis.caption: Closer to A+ and farther from A− gives a higher C.
topsis.projectionNote: Drawn on the two heaviest criteria; D and C use all criteria.
topsis.planeCaption: Top left is best. C is the same along each ray.

steps.s1: Each alternative is a point: its weighted normalized values on two criteria.
steps.s2: The ideal A+ takes the best value of each criterion, the anti-ideal A− the worst.
steps.s3: D+ and D− are the selected alternative's distances to the ideal and the anti-ideal.
steps.s4: Place each alternative at (D+, D−): its two distances become its coordinates.
steps.s5: Relative closeness C = D− / (D+ + D−) is the same along each ray; top left is best.

steps.s1: Contrast: σ, the standard deviation of each criterion's normalized values.
steps.s2: Conflict: Σ(1 − ρ) is large when a criterion correlates weakly or negatively with the others.
steps.s3: Information content C = σ × Σ(1 − ρ): a criterion that varies and disagrees carries more.
steps.s4: Weight w = C / ΣC: the same bars divided by the total, so the weights add up to 1.

entropy.title: Uneven shares, more weight
entropy.caption: Each bar is one alternative's share of the column total.

steps.s1: Shares: each bar is one alternative's share of the column. The dashed line is an even split.
steps.s2: Entropy e: the more even the shares, the closer e is to 1.
steps.s3: 1 − e is the information an even column lacks; the uneven criterion has more of it.
steps.s4: Weight w: 1 − e divided by the total over all criteria.

equal.title: Equal share 1/n for every criterion
equal.caption: Five smartphone criteria: the unit total 1 is divided by n = 5, so every criterion receives w = 1/5 = 0.2000 regardless of its column values.

steps.s1: The smartphone problem has n = 5 criteria on a 0 to 1 weight track, and equal weighting reads only the count n rather than the decision matrix or pairwise judgments.
steps.s2: The vertical dashed reference line marks 1/n = 1/5 of the unit total, and every criterion's bar reaches that exact mark.
steps.s3: Every criterion receives the same weight w = 0.2000, summing to 1 with no parameter to tune and no single criterion highlighted above the rest.

saw.title: Every part of the score has a criterion
saw.caption: Each segment is one criterion's weight times its normalized value; the bar ends at S.

steps.s1: Rescale: every value goes onto one 0 to 1 scale (r), so criteria can be added.
steps.s2: Weight: each part is multiplied by its criterion's weight; important criteria take more of the bar.
steps.s3: Add up: the bar ends at the score S, and the longest bar ranks first.

vikor.title: Group utility or the largest regret: v sets the balance
vikor.caption: Below the dashed line Q stays within DQ of the leader; without an acceptable advantage those alternatives form the compromise set.

steps.s1: Each alternative sits in the rescaled (S, R) plane: group utility on the horizontal axis, individual regret on the vertical axis, and the ideal at the bottom-left corner (0, 0).
steps.s2: Strategy weight v = 0.5 tilts the dashed iso-Q threshold line Q(a') + DQ; alternatives inside the shaded triangle below it stay within DQ of the leader.
steps.s3: The right-hand bars rank all alternatives by Q = v(S − S*) / (S− − S*) + (1 − v)(R − R*) / (R− − R*) and check acceptable advantage (C1) and acceptable stability (C2) to name the compromise set.

edas.title: Better or worse than the average, criterion by criterion
edas.caption: Right of the line: weighted distance above the average; left: below it; AS divides each by the largest SP or SN.

steps.s1: Distance: right of the line is above the average, left is below it (PDA and NDA).
steps.s2: Weight: each distance is multiplied by its criterion's weight; the stacks end at SP and SN.
steps.s3: Appraisal: AS joins SP and SN in one score; the highest AS ranks first.

sd.title: Wider spread, more weight
sd.caption: Each dot is one alternative on the 0 to 1 scale; the ruler under the dots is σ.

steps.s1: Each dot is one alternative's value, min-max scaled to 0 to 1.
steps.s2: Spread σ: the standard deviation of the dots, drawn from 0 on the same scale.
steps.s3: Weight w = σ / Σσ: the ruler is divided by the total, so the weights add up to 1.

merec.title: Remove a criterion, see how much the scores drop
merec.caption: Each segment is one alternative's drop in overall performance when the criterion is removed; together they make E.

steps.s1: Each row is a criterion. Remove it and see what happens to the scores.
steps.s2: Drops: the part of each alternative's overall performance S that is lost without this criterion.
steps.s3: The drops add up to the removal effect E.
steps.s4: Weight w = E / ΣE: the share of the total effect, so the weights add up to 1.

lopcow.title: Log ratio of root-mean-square to spread gives the weight
lopcow.caption: Each dot is one city on the 0 to 1 scale; the upper ruler is RMS, the lower ruler is sample σ.

steps.s1: Each dot is one city's value, min-max scaled to 0 to 1; the upper ruler from 0 is its root-mean-square RMS.
steps.s2: Spread σ: the sample standard deviation (divisor m - 1), drawn from 0 below RMS on the same scale.
steps.s3: Percentage value PV = |ln(RMS / σ) × 100|: the log gap between the two rulers.
steps.s4: Weight w = PV / ΣPV: the share of the total percentage value, so the weights add up to 1.

cilos.title: Smaller loss under other winners, more weight
cilos.caption: Each segment is the relative loss p_ij on a criterion when another criterion's best elderate is picked; their sum is |f_jj|, and F w = 0 gives the weights.

steps.s1: Each row is a criterion, and each criterion has a winning elderate with the largest normalized share.
steps.s2: Losses p_ij: the relative share a criterion loses when another criterion's winning elderate is chosen instead of its own.
steps.s3: The losses in a column add up to |f_jj|, the diagonal magnitude of the system matrix F.
steps.s4: Weight w solves F w = 0 with Σw = 1: a criterion that loses less under other winners gets a larger weight.

waspas.title: Sum or product: λ sets the blend
waspas.caption: Each line is one alternative; where two lines cross, they swap places. The vertical line marks λ = 0.5.

steps.s1: Each alternative's score Q(λ) = λ Q₁ + (1 − λ) Q₂ is a straight line from the weighted product Q₂ at λ = 0 to the weighted sum Q₁ at λ = 1.
steps.s2: Wherever two straight lines cross, those two alternatives swap ranks at that exact blend λ.
steps.s3: The vertical cursor marks the chosen blend λ = 0.5, reading each alternative's combined score Q and highlighting the leader.

copras.title: Benefit share plus a bonus for low cost
copras.caption: Each bar is S+ (benefit share) plus the cost bonus, which grows as the cost share S- shrinks; it ends at Q, then N in percent of the best.

steps.s1: Benefit share S+: each bar is the alternative's share of the benefit criteria.
steps.s2: Cost bonus: the smaller the cost share S− (printed), the longer the bonus.
steps.s3: Q = S+ plus the bonus; the longest bar ranks first.
steps.s4: N: each Q as a percent of the best Q.

marcos.title: Two imaginary rows to measure against
marcos.caption: The dashed rows are imaginary: the best and the worst value of every criterion. K- is a bar against the anti-ideal, K+ against the ideal; f(K) on the right.
marcos.sawCaption: Every dot lies on one line through 0, so no two alternatives can swap places.

steps.s1: Weighted totals S: each bar is an alternative's weighted sum, all on one scale.
steps.s2: Two imaginary rows: the ideal AI (best of every criterion) and the anti-ideal AAI (worst) mark the ends.
steps.s3: Utility f(K): each bar is read against both rows (K− and K+); the highest f(K) ranks first.

cocoso.title: Two scores, three readings
cocoso.caption: ka is the share of the total, kb the size against the weakest provider, kc a λ-mix against the best; k combines the three.
cocoso.lambdaCaption: λ moves only kc, so the lines barely bend: here no two providers swap at any λ.

steps.s1: ka: each provider's share of the total of S and P.
steps.s2: kb: how far each stands above the weakest provider.
steps.s3: kc: how each compares with the best mix of S and P.
steps.s4: k combines the three readings; the longest bar ranks first.

mabac.title: One border per criterion
mabac.caption: The line in every row is the border G, the geometric mean of the forklifts. Upper area: above it, lower area: below; S adds the sticks up.
mabac.sumTitle: Same order as a min-max weighted sum
mabac.sumCaption: Every dot sits on one line, so no two forklifts can swap; G only decides the sign of S.

steps.s1: The line in each row is the border G; above it is the upper area, below it the lower one.
steps.s2: Each criterion's distance from G is a stick: up if the forklift is better than G, down if worse.
steps.s3: Add the sticks up: the bar is the score S, and the highest S ranks first.

bwm.title: Two rulers, one scale
bwm.caption: Filled marks place each criterion by the answers about the best criterion, hollow marks by the answers about the worst; the dot is the weight, in times the worst criterion's weight; here every answer stays within the consistency threshold (CR {{cr}}, threshold {{threshold}}), so the workbench would not warn.

steps.s1: First the two anchors: the most important criterion and the least important one, and how many times more important the first is.
steps.s2: Each "best is x times more important than this one" puts the criterion somewhere on the scale.
steps.s3: The answers about the worst criterion place it a second time. Where the two places differ, your answers disagree; the marked one fits worst.
steps.s4: BWM picks the weights that keep the largest of these gaps as small as possible.

ahp.title: A matrix of ratios, one vector that fits it
ahp.caption: Upper cells hold the comparisons, lower cells their reciprocals, and the bars on the right show the eigenvector weights (CR {{cr}}, threshold {{threshold}}).

steps.s1: Each cell answers how many times more important the row is than the column; you fill the upper half and the lower half is its mirror.
steps.s2: If the answers were perfectly consistent, every cell would equal w_row / w_col: one set of weights would explain the whole table.
steps.s3: AHP finds the weights that fit the table best (the principal eigenvector) and draws them as bars.
steps.s4: Where an answer and its fitted ratio disagree most, the cell is marked; the consistency ratio CR summarizes all disagreements against the 0.10 limit.

moora.title: Benefit ratios pulling right, cost ratios pulling left
moora.caption: Right of the zero line: weighted benefit ratios adding to S+; left: weighted cost ratios adding to S-; y = S+ - S-.

steps.s1: Normalize: divide each value by its column length, benefit ratios to the right of 0 and cost ratios to the left.
steps.s2: Weight: multiply each ratio by its criterion weight; the stacks end at S+ and S-.
steps.s3: Subtract: y = S+ - S- is the net score, and the highest y ranks first.

aras.title: Share of the optimal row
aras.caption: The dashed row is A₀: the best value of every criterion, normalized in the same m + 1 column totals. Each bar is S, read against S₀; K = S / S₀ on the right.

steps.s1: Optimality S: each bar is an alternative's weighted sum of the m + 1 column shares.
steps.s2: Optimal row A₀: the column-best values get their own total S₀ on the same scale.
steps.s3: Utility degree K = S / S₀: each bar is divided by S₀, and the highest K ranks first.

codas.title: Two distances from the worst point, one pairwise score
codas.caption: Each supplier is measured from the negative-ideal point ns by Euclidean distance E and Taxicab distance T; H sums the pairwise margins.

steps.s1: Euclidean distance E: how far each supplier stands from the negative-ideal point ns.
steps.s2: Taxicab distance T: the sum of criterion gaps from ns, added when the Euclidean gap is at least τ.
steps.s3: Assessment score H: the row sum of pairwise comparisons; the highest H ranks first.

roc.title: Ordinal ranks become cardinal weights
roc.caption: Circles mark ROC (simplex centroid), squares mark RS (linear) and diamonds mark RR (reciprocal) on the same scale; the bars on the right show the active formula's weights.

steps.s1: Order the criteria from rank 1 (most important) to rank n (least important); the circle shows the ROC harmonic centroid weight.
steps.s2: Compare the three rank-order rules on one scale: RS (square) decays linearly, RR (diamond) concentrates steepest on rank 1, and ROC sits at the simplex centroid between them.
steps.s3: The chosen formula turns each criterion's rank into its weight bar w on the right, summing to 1.

promethee-ii.title: Leaving flow, entering flow, and net outranking flow
promethee-ii.caption: Each laptop model is compared pair by pair across criteria: leaving flow φ⁺ (how much it beats others) minus entering flow φ⁻ (how much others beat it) gives the net flow φ.

steps.s1: Leaving flow φ⁺: the row average of pairwise preference degrees, showing how strongly each model beats the others.
steps.s2: Entering flow φ⁻: the column average of pairwise preference degrees, showing how strongly the others beat each model.
steps.s3: Net flow φ = φ⁺ - φ⁻: leaving minus entering flow around zero; the highest φ ranks first.

swara.title: Step-down ratios chain into criterion weights
swara.caption: Starting from q₁ = 1 on the most important criterion, each next criterion divides the previous q by k_j = 1 + s_j; the bars on the right normalize q into weights w summing to 1.

steps.s1: Order the criteria from most to least important and state each step-down ratio s_j (0 for the first criterion) to form the coefficient k_j = 1 + s_j.
steps.s2: Chain the recalculated weights from q₁ = 1 by dividing each previous value by k_j: q_j = q_{j-1} / (1 + s_j).
steps.s3: Divide each q_j by the total Σq so the final weight bars w on the right sum to 1.

electre-i.title: Concordance majority, discordance veto, and outranking kernel
electre-i.caption: Each Galway plant site is compared pair by pair: net concordance Cₐ and net discordance Dₐ summarize pairwise support and opposition, [K] marks the non-outranked kernel after condensing the {A2, A3} cycle, and Φ orders the sites.

steps.s1: Concordance Cₐ and discordance Dₐ: for each site, sum how strongly it beats rivals on weighted criteria versus its largest scaled deficit.
steps.s2: Outranking kernel K: pairs with C ≥ 0.75 and D ≤ 0.50 form the outranking graph; condensing the {A2, A3} cycle leaves the kernel {A2, A3, A5} marked with [K].
steps.s3: Net outranking score Φ = (Cₐ - Dₐ) / (2(m - 1)): combines high net concordance and low net discordance into a complete ranking.

electre-iii.title: Descending distillation, ascending distillation, and net credibility
electre-iii.caption: Each waste treatment option is compared by fuzzy credibility σ(a, b): descending distillation r↓ selects from the top down, ascending distillation r↑ eliminates from the bottom up, and Φ shows net credibility.

steps.s1: Descending rank r↓: iterative qualification from the highest credibility cut down, picking the strongest options first.
steps.s2: Ascending rank r↑: iterative elimination from the weakest options up; where r↓ and r↑ disagree, the pair is incomparable.
steps.s3: Net credibility Φ: leaving minus entering credibility around zero; options are ordered by average distillation rank (r↓ + r↑) / 2, with Φ breaking ties.

critic.normalized: Min-max normalization: each column is rescaled to the range 0 to 1, with cost criteria reversed so that 1 is always the best value.
critic.sigma: Contrast: the sample standard deviation of each normalized column.
critic.correlation: Conflict between criteria: the Pearson correlation of every pair of normalized columns.
critic.conflict: Total conflict of each criterion: the sum of 1 minus its correlation with every criterion.
critic.information: Information content of each criterion: its standard deviation times its total conflict.
critic.informationTotal: Total information content over all criteria.
critic.weights: Weights: each criterion's share of the total information content.

entropy.normalized: Min-max normalization: each column is rescaled to the range 0 to 1, with cost criteria reversed so that 1 is always the best value.
entropy.proportionsSum: Shares: each raw value divided by its column's total. Criterion types are not used.
entropy.proportionsMinmax: Shares: each normalized value divided by its column's total.
entropy.entropy: Entropy of each criterion: 1 when the shares are equal, lower the more uneven they are.
entropy.diversification: Degree of diversification: 1 minus the entropy, the information a criterion carries.
entropy.weights: Entropy weights: each criterion's share of the total diversification.

topsis.normalized: Vector normalization: each value divided by the length of its column.
topsis.weighted: Weighted normalized matrix: each column multiplied by its weight.
topsis.idealBest: Ideal solution A+: the best weighted value on each criterion (the maximum for benefit, the minimum for cost).
topsis.idealWorst: Anti-ideal solution A-: the worst weighted value on each criterion.
topsis.distanceBest: Euclidean distance D+ of each alternative from the ideal solution.
topsis.distanceWorst: Euclidean distance D- of each alternative from the anti-ideal solution.
topsis.closeness: Closeness coefficient C = D- / (D+ + D-). A higher value ranks higher.

equal.weights: Equal weights: every criterion gets 1 / n.

saw.normalizedLinearMax: Linear max normalization: each value divided by the column maximum, or for a cost criterion the column minimum divided by the value, so the best value is 1.
saw.normalizedSum: Sum normalization: each value divided by its column total; a cost criterion uses 1 / x first, so the shares add up to 1.
saw.weighted: Contributions: each normalized value multiplied by its criterion weight.
saw.scores: Score S: the sum of an alternative's contributions. A higher value ranks higher.

vikor.best: Best value f* of each criterion: the maximum for a benefit, the minimum for a cost.
vikor.worst: Worst value f− of each criterion: the other end of its column.
vikor.weightedDistance: Weighted distance d to the best value: 0 at the best, the criterion weight at the worst.
vikor.groupUtility: Group utility S: the sum of an alternative's distances. A lower value is better.
vikor.individualRegret: Individual regret R: an alternative's largest single distance. A lower value is better.
vikor.q: Compromise index Q: S and R rescaled to 0 to 1 and mixed by v. A lower value ranks higher.
vikor.threshold: Advantage threshold DQ = 1 / (m - 1): the Q gap the first alternative needs over the second.

edas.average: Average solution AV: the mean of each criterion over all alternatives.
edas.pda: Positive distance PDA: how much better than the average an alternative is, as a share of the average.
edas.nda: Negative distance NDA: how much worse than the average an alternative is, as a share of the average.
edas.weightedPda: Weighted positive distances w PDA: what each criterion adds to SP.
edas.weightedNda: Weighted negative distances w NDA: what each criterion adds to SN.
edas.sp: SP: the sum of an alternative's weighted positive distances.
edas.sn: SN: the sum of an alternative's weighted negative distances.
edas.nsp: NSP = SP / max SP: 1 for the alternative furthest above the average.
edas.nsn: NSN = 1 - SN / max SN: 0 for the alternative furthest below the average.
edas.scores: Appraisal score AS = (NSP + NSN) / 2. A higher value ranks higher.

sd.normalized: Min-max normalization: each column is rescaled to the range 0 to 1, with cost criteria reversed so that 1 is always the best value.
sd.sigma: Spread: the sample standard deviation of each normalized column.
sd.weights: Weights: each criterion's share of the total spread.

merec.normalized: Normalization to smaller is better: benefit min / x, cost x / max, so the worst value of each column is 1 and the best the smallest.
merec.absLog: Absolute logarithm of each normalized value: 0 for the worst value, larger the better the value.
merec.performance: Overall performance of each alternative: ln(1 + the mean of its absolute logarithms over all criteria).
merec.performanceRemoved: Performance with one criterion removed: the same sum without that criterion, still divided by the number of criteria.
merec.removalEffect: Removal effect: the total drop in performance over all alternatives when the criterion is removed.
merec.weights: MEREC weights: each criterion's share of the total removal effect.

lopcow.normalized: Min-max normalization: each column is rescaled to the range 0 to 1, with cost criteria reversed so that 1 is always the best value.
lopcow.rms: Root-mean-square RMS: the square root of the mean of squared normalized values in each column.
lopcow.stdDev: Spread σ: the sample standard deviation (divisor m - 1) of each normalized column.
lopcow.pv: Percentage value PV: the absolute natural logarithm of RMS over σ, multiplied by 100.
lopcow.weights: LOPCOW weights: each criterion's share of the total percentage value.

cilos.normalized: Sum normalization: cost criteria are inverted with min x / x first, then each value is divided by its column total so the shares add up to 1.
cilos.squareMatrix: Square matrix A: row i copies the normalized row of the alternative that reaches the maximum on criterion i.
cilos.lossMatrix: Relative impact-loss matrix P: how much criterion j loses relative to its maximum a_jj when criterion i's winning alternative is chosen.
cilos.systemMatrix: Loss system matrix F: P with each diagonal entry set to the negative sum of its column, so every column of F adds up to 0.
cilos.weights: CILOS weights: the unique vector w with sum 1 that solves the homogeneous linear system F w = 0.

waspas.normalized: Linear max normalization: each value divided by the column maximum, or for a cost criterion the column minimum divided by the value, so the best value is 1.
waspas.wsm: Weighted sum Q1: each normalized value times its criterion weight, added up.
waspas.wpm: Weighted product Q2: each normalized value raised to its criterion weight, multiplied together. It is never above Q1.
waspas.scores: Score Q = λ Q1 + (1 - λ) Q2. A higher value ranks higher.
waspas.lambdaSweep: Q at λ = 0, 0.1, ..., 1: where two alternatives swap places as λ moves.

copras.normalizedSum: Shares r: each value divided by its column total, for benefit and cost criteria alike.
copras.weighted: Weighted shares d = w r: each column now adds up to its criterion weight.
copras.sPlus: Benefit sum S+: the weighted shares of the benefit criteria, added up.
copras.sMinus: Cost sum S-: the weighted shares of the cost criteria, added up; a smaller S- is better.
copras.significance: Relative significance Q = S+ plus the cost weight shared out in proportion to 1 / S-; a higher value ranks higher and the Q values add up to 1.
copras.utility: Utility degree N: Q as a percentage of the largest Q, so the best alternative has 100.

marcos.normalized: Normalized values n: each value against the ideal row AI (the column best), so the ideal gets 1; the same as SAW (Linear).
marcos.weighted: Weighted values v = w n: each normalized value times its criterion weight.
marcos.sAai: S_aai: the weighted total of the anti-ideal row AAI, the worst value of every criterion.
marcos.sAi: S_ai: the weighted total of the ideal row AI, which is the sum of the weights, 1.
marcos.s: Weighted total S of each alternative: the row sum of v, the same number as the SAW (Linear) score.
marcos.kMinus: Utility degree K- = S / S_aai: how many anti-ideals the alternative is worth.
marcos.kPlus: Utility degree K+ = S / S_ai: the share of the ideal the alternative reaches.
marcos.fKMinus: f(K-) = K+ / (K+ + K-): the same number for every alternative, so it is shown once.
marcos.fKPlus: f(K+) = K- / (K+ + K-): the same number for every alternative, so it is shown once.
marcos.utility: Utility f(K): K+ and K- merged by the two utility functions. A higher value ranks higher; since f(K) = c · S, the order is the order of S.

cocoso.normalized: Min-max normalization: the worst value of each column becomes 0 and the best 1, for a cost criterion the other way round. Negative values work too.
cocoso.s: Weighted sum S: each normalized value times its criterion weight, added up.
cocoso.p: Power sum P: each normalized value raised to its criterion weight, added up. A criterion with weight 0 is left out, since 0 to the power 0 would add 1 to every P.
cocoso.ka: ka: the share of S + P in the total over all alternatives.
cocoso.kb: kb: S and P each divided by the smallest one, added. It is at least 2; exactly 2 for an alternative with both the smallest S and the smallest P.
cocoso.kc: kc = (λ S + (1 - λ) P) / (λ max S + (1 - λ) max P). The best mix gets 1.
cocoso.scores: Combined score k = (ka kb kc)^(1/3) + (ka + kb + kc) / 3. A higher value ranks higher.
cocoso.lambdaSweep: k at λ = 0, 0.1, ..., 1: where two alternatives swap places as λ moves.

mabac.normalized: Min-max normalization: the worst value of each column becomes 0 and the best 1, for a cost criterion the other way round. Negative and zero values are fine too.
mabac.weighted: Weighted matrix V: each normalized value plus 1, times its criterion weight, so it lies between w and 2w.
mabac.border: Border G: the geometric mean of each column of V, computed through logarithms so that hundreds of alternatives do not underflow to 0.
mabac.distance: Distance Q = V - G: positive in the upper area (towards the best value), negative in the lower area.
mabac.scores: Distance to border S: the row sum of Q. A higher value ranks higher; S is the min-max weighted sum minus one constant, so the order is that sum's.

bwm.bestToOthers: Best over others: how much more important the best criterion is than each, 1‑9.
bwm.othersToWorst: Others over worst: how much more important each criterion is than the worst, 1‑9.
bwm.consistencyLocal: Consistency per criterion: how far a_Bj times a_jW is from a_BW.
bwm.xi: Deviation: the largest gap between the answers and the fitted weights.
bwm.weights: BWM weights: the linear model, solved in closed form, summing to 1.

ahp.pairwiseMatrix: Pairwise comparison matrix: upper-triangle answers with reciprocal lower half and 1 on the diagonal.
ahp.lambdaMax: Principal eigenvalue λmax: the average ratio of each weighted row sum (Aw)_i to its weight w_i.
ahp.consistencyIndex: Consistency index CI = (λmax - n) / (n - 1): 0 when the comparisons are perfectly consistent.
ahp.consistencyRatio: Consistency ratio CR = CI / RI_n: compares CI against Saaty's random index; up to 0.10 is the usual limit.
ahp.weights: AHP weights: the normalized priority vector from the principal eigenvector or the row geometric mean.

ahpRanking.local: Local priorities p: column shares from the table (1 / x for cost) or the priority vector of the criterion's pairwise comparison matrix.
ahpRanking.weighted: Weighted local priorities v = w p: each alternative's local priority multiplied by the criterion weight.
ahpRanking.scores: Global priority P: the sum of an alternative's weighted local priorities across all criteria, summing to 1.

moora.normalized: Vector normalization: each value divided by the Euclidean length of its column.
moora.weighted: Weighted normalized matrix v: each normalized ratio multiplied by its criterion weight.
moora.benefitSum: Benefit sum S+: the weighted ratios of the benefit criteria, added up.
moora.costSum: Cost sum S-: the weighted ratios of the cost criteria, added up.
moora.score: Net assessment score y = S+ - S-. A higher value ranks higher, and negative values are normal when cost weights dominate.

aras.optimalRow: Optimal row A₀: the best value of each criterion (the maximum for a benefit, the minimum for a cost), prepended before normalizing.
aras.normalized: Normalized shares x̄: cost criteria are inverted with 1 / x, then each value is divided by the total of all m + 1 rows (A₀ plus the m alternatives).
aras.weighted: Weighted shares x̂ = w x̄: each normalized share multiplied by its criterion weight.
aras.optimalScore: Optimal score S₀: the weighted row sum of the optimal row A₀, the benchmark for every alternative.
aras.optimality: Optimality function S: the weighted row sum of each alternative.
aras.utilityDegree: Utility degree K = S / S₀: each alternative's optimality divided by the optimal score. A higher value ranks higher.

codas.normalized: Linear max normalization: each value divided by the column maximum, or for a cost criterion the column minimum divided by the value, so the best value is 1.
codas.weighted: Weighted normalized matrix r = w n: each normalized value multiplied by its criterion weight.
codas.negativeIdeal: Negative-ideal solution ns: the smallest weighted value in each criterion column.
codas.euclidean: Euclidean distance E of each alternative from the negative-ideal solution.
codas.taxicab: Taxicab distance T: the sum of absolute differences from the negative-ideal solution.
codas.relativeAssessment: Relative assessment matrix Ra: for each pair (i, k), (E_i - E_k) plus (T_i - T_k) when |E_i - E_k| is at least τ.
codas.score: Assessment score H: the row sum of Ra. A higher value ranks higher, and the scores sum to 0.

roc.ranks: Criterion ranks r from 1 (most important) to n (least important).
roc.weights: Rank-order weights w from the selected formula (ROC centroid, Rank Sum or Rank Reciprocal), summing to 1.

swara.s: Comparative importance ratio s_j stating how much less important criterion j is than criterion j - 1 (0 for the first criterion).
swara.k: Step coefficient k_j = 1 + s_j (1 for the most important criterion).
swara.q: Recalculated weight q_j = q_{j-1} / k_j, chaining the step-down ratios from q_1 = 1.
swara.weights: Normalized SWARA weights w_j = q_j / Σq_r, summing to 1.

promethee-ii.preferenceMatrix: Aggregated preference matrix π: for each ordered pair (a, b), the weighted sum of unicriterion preference degrees P_j(a, b).
promethee-ii.positiveFlow: Leaving (positive) flow φ⁺: the row average of π over all other alternatives, measuring how strongly each alternative outranks the rest.
promethee-ii.negativeFlow: Entering (negative) flow φ⁻: the column average of π over all other alternatives, measuring how strongly the rest outrank each alternative.
promethee-ii.netFlow: Net outranking flow φ = φ⁺ - φ⁻: a higher value ranks higher, and the net flows sum to 0.

electre-i.oriented: Oriented matrix g: benefit criteria stay as given and cost criteria are negated so larger values are always better.
electre-i.concordance: Concordance matrix C: for each pair (a, b), the share of total weight on criteria where a is at least as good as b.
electre-i.discordance: Discordance matrix D: for each pair (a, b), the largest scaled deficit where a falls behind b on any criterion.
electre-i.outranking: Outranking matrix S: S(a, b) = 1 when C(a, b) ≥ ĉ and D(a, b) ≤ d̂.
electre-i.kernel: Kernel membership K: 1 for alternatives in the outranking kernel after condensing mutual outranking cycles, 0 otherwise.
electre-i.netConcordance: Net concordance Cₐ: outgoing minus incoming concordance across all other alternatives.
electre-i.netDiscordance: Net discordance Dₐ: outgoing minus incoming discordance across all other alternatives; lower values are better.
electre-i.netScore: Net outranking score Φ = (Cₐ - Dₐ) / (2(m - 1)): normalized net concordance minus net discordance in [-1, 1].

electre-iii.concordance: Concordance matrix C: for each ordered pair (a, b), the weighted sum of unicriterion concordance degrees c_j(a, b) from the indifference and preference thresholds.
electre-iii.credibility: Credibility matrix σ: concordance C(a, b) attenuated by any criterion whose discordance d_j(a, b) exceeds C(a, b); a veto deficit reduces σ(a, b) to 0.
electre-iii.descending: Descending distillation rank r↓: competition rank from top-down qualification on the credibility matrix.
electre-iii.ascending: Ascending distillation rank r↑: competition rank from bottom-up elimination on the credibility matrix.
electre-iii.netCredibility: Net credibility flow Φ: leaving minus entering credibility average over all other alternatives.

codes.alternatives-count-mismatch: The number of alternative names does not match the number of rows.
codes.value-out-of-range: {{alternative}} on {{criterion}} is too large or too small to compute with. Rescale {{criterion}} (another unit) so its values lie between 10⁻¹⁰⁰ and 10¹⁰⁰.
codes.constant-column: Every alternative has the same value on {{criterion}}, so it cannot tell them apart.
codes.non-positive-value: {{alternative}} on {{criterion}} is {{value}}. This method divides by the values or takes their logarithm, so each must be above 0.
codes.negative-value: {{alternative}} on {{criterion}} is {{value}}. Raw data (sum) needs values of 0 or more; choose Min-max to use negative values.
codes.invalid-weight: Enter a number for the weight of {{criterion}}.
codes.negative-weight: The weight of {{criterion}} is {{value}}. Weights cannot be negative.
codes.weights-sum: Weights sum to {{value}}, they must sum to 1.
codes.non-positive-average: The average of {{criterion}} is {{value}}. EDAS divides by each criterion's average, so it must be above 0.
codes.all-worst-alternative: {{alternative}} is the worst on every weighted criterion, so its S and P are 0 and CoCoSo would divide by 0. Remove it or choose another method.
codes.judgements-incomplete: {{value}} of the questions answered; answer the rest to get the weights.
codes.alt-judgements-incomplete: On {{criterion}}, {{value}} of {{total}} alternative comparisons are answered; answer the rest to compute the ranking.
codes.anchors-missing: Choose the best and the worst criterion first.

critic.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so its CRITIC weight is 0.
critic.few-alternatives: With fewer than 4 alternatives the correlations are unstable. Read the CRITIC weights with care.
critic.no-conflict-equal-weights: The criteria that vary carry no conflict with each other (only one varies, or they move together), so they share the weight equally.
critic.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so there is no information to weigh. Equal weights are used instead.
critic.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full weight. Check whether the difference is real.

entropy.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so its Entropy weight is 0.
entropy.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet Entropy gives it a weight. Check whether the difference is real.
entropy.zeros-in-column: {{criterion}} contains zeros, which can inflate its weight.
entropy.two-alternatives-minmax: With 2 alternatives, min-max gives every criterion that is not constant the same weight.
entropy.dominant-weight: {{criterion}} takes more than half of the weight, so check whether its spread is real.
entropy.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so equal weights are used instead.

topsis.zero-column: Every value of {{criterion}} is 0, so it does not affect the ranking.
topsis.zero-distance: Some alternatives coincide with both the ideal and the anti-ideal solution. They get a closeness of 0.5.

vikor.constant-column: Every value of {{criterion}} is the same, so it adds nothing to S or R.
vikor.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full distance. Check whether the difference is real.
vikor.equal-group-utility: Every alternative has the same S, so Q comes from R alone and reaches at most 1 − v, which can make C1 harder to meet.
vikor.equal-regret: Every alternative has the same R, so Q comes from S alone and reaches at most v, which can make C1 harder to meet.
vikor.no-spread: Every alternative has the same S and the same R, so all get Q = 0.
vikor.tie-for-first: More than one alternative has the lowest Q; they are listed in input order and all are in the compromise set.

edas.constant-column: Every value of {{criterion}} is the same, so it adds nothing to SP or SN.
edas.negative-values: {{criterion}} has negative values. EDAS measures distance as a share of the average, so the result depends on where zero is.
edas.small-average: The average of {{criterion}} is close to 0 next to its values, so its distances grow very large and it can decide the ranking even with a small weight.
edas.no-spread: No alternative is above or below the average on a weighted criterion, so every alternative gets AS = 0.5.

sd.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so its SD weight is 0.
sd.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full weight. Check whether the difference is real.
sd.two-alternatives: With 2 alternatives, every criterion that is not constant gets the same SD weight.
sd.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so equal weights are used instead.

merec.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so removing it changes nothing and its MEREC weight is 0.
merec.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so equal weights are used instead.
merec.dominant-weight: {{criterion}} takes more than half of the weight, so check that its range is real.
merec.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet MEREC gives it a removal effect. Check whether the difference is real.

lopcow.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so its LOPCOW weight is 0.
lopcow.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full weight. Check whether the difference is real.
lopcow.two-alternatives: With 2 alternatives, every varying column has RMS equal to its sample standard deviation (PV = 0), so equal weights are used instead.
lopcow.zero-pv-column: {{criterion}} has RMS equal to its sample standard deviation (PV = 0), so its LOPCOW weight is 0.
lopcow.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so equal weights are used instead.

cilos.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so its CILOS weight is 0.
cilos.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet CILOS normalizes its tiny losses against the rest of the system. Check whether the difference is real.
cilos.shared-optimum: Two or more criteria reach their best value on the same alternative, so the corresponding rows of A coincide and the relative loss between them is 0.
cilos.zero-loss-equal-weights: One alternative is simultaneously the best on every varying criterion (or the loss system is degenerate), so all relative losses vanish (P = 0, F = 0) and active criteria share the weight equally.
cilos.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so equal weights are used instead.

copras.no-cost-criteria: There is no cost criterion with a weight above 0, so Q = S+ and COPRAS gives the same result as SAW with the sum option.

cocoso.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full weight. Check whether the difference is real.
cocoso.no-spread: Every active criterion is constant, so all alternatives tie at rank 1.

mabac.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full weight. Check whether the difference is real.

bwm.inconsistent: Answers about {{criterion}} fit worst; the weights are still computed.
bwm.threshold-approximate: With more than 9 criteria the consistency threshold is approximate (the 9-criteria value).

ahp.inconsistent: The consistency ratio CR is at or above 0.10; check the highlighted pair, though the weights are still computed.
ahp.inconsistent-criterion: On {{criterion}}, the consistency ratio CR is at or above 0.10; check the highlighted pair, though the priorities are still computed.
ahp.many-criteria: With 8 or more criteria AHP asks at least 28 comparisons and consistency is harder to keep; consider BWM for fewer questions.

ahp-ranking.pairwise-ignored-above-cap: With more than 7 alternatives, pairwise alternative comparisons are ignored and local priorities come from the decision matrix.

promethee-ii.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet preference functions rescale it to 0 to 1. Check whether the difference is real.

electre-i.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet range discordance rescales it to 0 to 1. Check whether the difference is real.
electre-i.cycle-detected: Mutual outranking cycles exist in S; each cycle is condensed into an equivalence class before finding the kernel K.
electre-i.non-kernel-leader: The alternative with the highest net score is outside the outranking kernel K; check the kernel column as well.

moora.zero-column: Every value of {{criterion}} is 0, so it does not affect the ranking.
